titulo: AI Shockwaves and Midterm Shifts Grip Global Markets
resumo: November 2026 brought intense volatility to global financial markets, driven by a dramatic political shift in the United States and severe turbulence within the artificial intelligence sector. **The S&P 500 fell -5% this month**, weighed down by a historic tech sell-off and mounting questions over the sustainability of massive AI infrastructure spending. Meanwhile, geopolitical optimism provided some relief as **crude oil prices tumbled -23.6%**, closing the month at 91.8 USD a barrel on hopes of de-escalation in the Middle East. **Investors rushed to safe havens**, pushing equity volatility sharply higher as markets grappled with a rapidly evolving regulatory and corporate landscape.

sumup.frase: Markets face severe turbulence as **AI scandals** and political shifts spark intense **volatility**.
sumup.porque: Uncertainty surrounding political shifts and tech sector shocks kept market participants on high alert.

drivers.texto: The Democratic sweep of Congress upended investor expectations, triggering regulatory fears and sparking a historic tech-led market rout that erased trillions in valuation.
The abrupt resignation of CEO Jensen Huang amid an investigation into China-related ties sent shockwaves through the semiconductor industry and broader AI market.

drivers.factor: Crude Oil Plunges on Peace Hopes
drivers.texto: Hopes of diplomatic progress in US-Iran talks drove Brent crude down by -23.6% over the month to settle at 91.8 USD a barrel, easing broader cost pressures.

drivers.factor: Hot US Inflation Sparks Rate Fears
drivers.texto: Higher-than-expected inflation prints reignited market chatter over potential Federal Reserve rate hikes, sending US Treasury yields higher and pressuring risk assets.

themes.texto: The extraordinary capital expenditure boom underpinning artificial intelligence faced its first major reality check, as soaring power, memory, and regulatory costs spooked investors. Corporate spending commitments remained massive, highlighted by Anthropic targeting a blockbuster IPO valuation of up to $1.4 trillion, yet high-profile stumbles exposed deep vulnerabilities in the tech supply chain. Markets are increasingly debating whether future revenue growth can justify the trillions being poured into data centres and advanced computing.

Persistent price pressures continued to challenge monetary authorities globally, keeping borrowing costs elevated for households and businesses alike. While the European Central Bank maintained its deposit rate at 2.5%, the Bank of England enacted a rate rise to 4%, its first increase in over three years. In the US, hot consumer price data revived debate over whether central banks might be forced to implement further tightening cycles to cool resilient demand.

Easing tensions in the Middle East provided a welcome reprieve for energy-importing nations, driving a steep correction in global petroleum markets. The sharp decline in oil prices helped alleviate headline inflation worries, though regional conflicts and supply chain vulnerabilities continued to cast a shadow over industrial output and transportation costs across Europe and North America.

questoes.q: Will Nvidia recover its market dominance after the departure of Jensen Huang?
questoes.porque: Huang was widely seen as the visionary force behind the company's meteoric rise to a multi-trillion-dollar valuation.
questoes.sinais: Upcoming earnings reports and clarity on permanent leadership and regulatory probes will provide direction.

questoes.q: Are central banks finished raising interest rates in this cycle?
questoes.porque: Hotter inflation prints and robust labor markets have revived fears of additional monetary tightening.
questoes.sinais: Incoming consumer price indexes and central bank forward guidance will answer this debate.

questoes.q: Can Anthropic's blockbuster IPO succeed amid broader tech sector volatility?
questoes.porque: It serves as a crucial valuation benchmark for the entire generative AI ecosystem following historic market corrections.
questoes.sinais: Final pricing outcomes and institutional subscription levels during the flotation will be decisive.

momentos.facto: Marvell announced an 80 billion dollar deal to acquire Lumentum, fueling massive M&A activity in the tech sector.
Democrats swept Congress in the US midterm elections, triggering a powerful relief rally led by the Dow.
US tech stocks suffered their worst sell-off since the pandemic, wiping trillions off market values amid AI regulatory fears.
The Bank of England raised interest rates to 4%, marking its first increase in over three years.
Hot US inflation data sparked renewed rate-hike fears, sending bond yields sharply higher across global markets.
Nvidia shares plunged as CEO Jensen Huang officially resigned following an internal investigation into his conduct.
